source_text: Εʹ. Οὗτος, καὶ τὸν Ἑωσφόρον ἐσκότισε, καταπεσόντα δι' ἔπαρσιν· οὐ γὰρ ἤνεγκε, θεῖος ὢν, μὴ καὶ θεὸς νομισθῆναι· καὶ τὸν Ἀδὰμ ἐξέβαλε τοῦ παρα δείσου, δι' ἡδονῆς κλέψας καὶ γυναικός. Ἐπείσθη γὰρ, ὡς θεὸς εἶναι βασκαίνεται, τοῦ τῆς γνώσεως ξύλου τέως εἰργόμενος. Οὗτος καὶ τὸν Κάϊν ἀδελ φοκτόνον ἐποίησεν, οὐκ ἐνεγκόντα θυσίαν ὁσιω τέραν. Οὗτος καὶ ὕδατι κόσμον ἐκάλυψεν ἀκοσμοῦν τα, καὶ Σοδομίτας πυρὶ κατέκλυσεν. Οὗτος καὶ Δαθὰν καὶ Ἀβειρὼν κατέχωσε κατὰ Μωσέως μανέν-τας, καὶ Μαριὰμ ἐλέπρωσε κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ μόνον γογγύσασαν. Οὗτος καὶ προφητῶν αἵμασι τὴν γῆν ἐμίανε, καὶ Σολομῶντα γυναιξὶ κατέσεισε τὸν σοφώ τατον. Οὗτος καὶ Ἰούδαν προδότην ἀνέδειξεν, ἀργυ ρίῳ μικρῷ κλαπέντα, τὸν ἀγχόνης ἄξιον· καὶ Ἡρώ δην παιδοφόνον, καὶ Χριστοκτόνον Πιλᾶτον ἐδημιούργησεν. Οὗτος καὶ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ἐλίκμησε καὶ διέσπειρεν, ἐξ ἧς οὔπω καὶ νῦν ἀνανεύουσιν ἁμαρτίας. Οὗτος καὶ τὸν ἀποστάτην ἡμῖν ἐπανέστησε τύραν νον, οὗ καὶ νῦν ἔτι παραλυποῦσιν οἱ ἄνθρακες, εἰ καὶ τὴν φλόγα διαπεφεύγαμεν. Οὗτος καὶ τὸ καλὸν σῶμα τῆς Ἐκκλησίας κατέτεμεν, εἰς διαφόρους καὶ ἀντιπάλους σπουδὰς μερίσας. Οὗτος καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν Ἱεροβοὰμ ἐπανέστησε τὸν δοῦλον τῆς ἁμαρτίας, καὶ τῇ γλώσσῃ δεσμὸν ἐπιτίθησιν· οὐ γὰρ φέρει τὴν Τριάδα λαμπρυνομένην, καὶ ὅλῃ θεότητι λάμπου σαν, καὶ τιμίους ποιοῦσαν ὑμῖν τοὺς γνησίους ἑαυτῆς κήρυκας. Ἆρα φλυαρεῖν ὑμῖν δοκοῦμεν, οὕ τως εἰκάζοντες; ἢ καὶ λίαν ὀρθῶς τοῦ πόθου τὰς αἰ τίας ὁ γραφεὺς λόγος ἀνεζωγράφησεν; Περὶ μὲν δὴ τούτων οὕτω γινώσκω. ς ʹ. Ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ ταῖς ὕβρεσιν ὁρῶ τινας δυσχεραίνοντας, καὶ συμφορὰν ἑαυτῶν ποιουμένους, τὴν ἀτιμίαν τὴν ἡμετέραν, φέρε, καὶ περὶ ταύτης βραχέα φι λοσοφήσωμεν. Ἐγὼ γὰρ, εἰ μὲν ἀνθρώπινόν τι καὶ μικρὸν ἐννοῶν, ἢ τῆς καθέδρας ταύτης μεταποιούμενος, ἢ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐπέστην ὑμῖν, μετὰ τῆς πολιᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τῶν ἐῤῥικνωμένων τούτων καὶ χρόνῳ καὶ νόσῳ μελῶν, ἢ νῦν ταύτας φέρω τὰς ἀτι μίας, αἰσχυνοίμην μὲν ἂν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, ἃ καὶ τοῖς παλαιοῖς ἔθος μαρτύρεσθαι· αἰσχυνοίμην δ' ἂν τὴν καθέδραν ταύτην, καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν τοῦτο συνέδριον, καὶ τὸν ἅγιον τοῦτον καὶ νεοπαγῆ λαὸν, ἐφ' ὃν τοσαύτη τῶν πονηρῶν δυνάμεων ἡ παράταξις, ἵνα πρὶν συστῆναι λυθῇ, καὶ πρὶν γεννηθῆναι νεκρωθῇ, κατὰ Χριστὸν ἤδη μορφούμενος. Αἰσχυνοίμην δ' ἂν τοὺς ἐμοὺς καμάτους καὶ πόνους, καὶ τὸ ἔσθημα τοῦτο τὸ τρύχινον, καὶ τὴν ἐρημίαν καὶ τὴν ἀναχώ ρησιν ᾗ συνεζήσαμεν, καὶ τὸν ἄσκευον βίον, καὶ τὴν εὐτελῆ τράπεζαν, μικρὸν τῶν πτηνῶν ἀποδέουσαν. Ἀληθευέτωσαν δὲ καί τινες περὶ ἡμῶν, ὅτι γυ ναικὸς ἀλλοτρίας ἐπεθυμήσαμεν, οἱ μηδὲ ἰδίαν ἔχειν θελήσαντες. Ἐχέτωσαν δὲ ἡμῶν καὶ Γαβαωνῖται πλέον, οὓς οὐδὲ εἰς ξυλοκόπους καὶ ὑδροφόρους οἶδ' ὅτι τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον παραδέχεται, μέχρις ἂν προσίωσι τοῖς ἱεροῖς μετὰ τοιούτων τοῦ βίου καὶ τοῦ λόγου στιγμάτων. Εἰ δὲ τῷ λόγῳ συνηγορήσοντες ἥκομεν, καὶ τῇ χήρᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνάν δρῳ τέως Ἐκκλησίᾳ τὰ δυνατὰ συνεισοίσοντες, οἶόν τινες ἐπίτροποι καὶ κηδεμόνες, ἄλλῳ νυμφαγω γήσοντες, ὃς ἐὰν ἄξιος τοῦ κάλλους φανῇ, καὶ πλείο να τὰ ἐξ ἀρετῆς ἔδνα προσενέγκῃ τῇ βασιλίδι, πότερον, ἐπαινετοὶ τῆς προθυμίας, ἢ ψεκτοὶ τῆς ὑπονοίας; ὅτι τοῖς ἀλλοτρίοις κρινόμεθα πάθεσιν.
thought_title: Envy through history and denial of seeking office
orientation: Gregory is speaking, continuing his catalogue of what envy does and then answering those embarrassed by the insults against him.
pass_a_gloss: This same thing also darkened the Morning-star, who fell through arrogance; for he did not bear, although divine, not also to be regarded as God; and it cast Adam out of paradise, having stolen him away through pleasure and a woman. For he was persuaded, while kept away for a time from the tree of knowledge, that he is begrudged being God. This same thing also made Cain a brother-murderer, for not bearing a more holy sacrifice. This same thing also covered with water a disorderly world, and flooded the Sodomites with fire. This same thing also buried Dathan and Abiram, who raged against Moses, and made Miriam leprous, who only murmured against her brother. This same thing also stained the earth with blood of prophets, and shook Solomon the wisest by women. This same thing also showed Judas to be a betrayer, stolen by a little silver, worthy of hanging; and it produced Herod as child-murderer, and Pilate as Christ-murderer. This same thing also winnowed Israel and scattered it, from which sin they have not yet even now recovered. This same thing also raised up against us the apostate tyrant, whose embers still even now cause lingering pain, although we have escaped the flame. This same thing also cut up the beautiful body of the church, dividing it into different and hostile parties. This same thing also raised up against us Jeroboam the slave of sin, and puts a bond on my tongue; for he does not bear the Trinity being glorified, and shining with the whole Godhead, and making her genuine heralds honored in your sight. Do we then seem to you to talk nonsense, judging so? Or has the written account quite rightly depicted the causes of the longing? Concerning these things then I know thus. Since I see some are also vexed at the insults, and making our dishonor their own misfortune, come, let us also discuss this briefly in a philosophical manner. For I, if indeed thinking some human and small thing, either laying claim to this see, or I came upon you as ruler, with this gray hair, and these limbs shriveled by both time and sickness, or now I bear these dishonors, I would be ashamed before heaven and earth, which even the ancients have custom to call as witnesses; I would be ashamed before this see, and this holy council, and this holy and newly formed people, against whom so great is the array of evil powers, so that before it stands together it may be dissolved, and before it is born it may be killed, being already formed according to Christ. I would be ashamed before my toils and labors, and this hairy garment, and the desert and the retirement with which we lived together, and the unfurnished life, and the cheap table, falling short little of birds. Let some also speak truthfully about us, that we desired another wife, we who did not wish to have even our own. Let the Gibeonites also have more hold on us, whom I know that the Holy Spirit does not admit even as woodcutters and watercarriers, until they approach holy things with such stains of life and speech. But if we came pleading for the word, and bringing in what we can for the widowed and presently husbandless church, like caretakers and guardians, to lead her as bride to another, who if he appears worthy of her beauty, and brings more bridal gifts from virtue to the queen, whether are we praiseworthy for eagerness, or blameworthy for suspicion? Because we are judged by passions alien to us.

lemmas.gloss: to lead as bride to another

choices.why: Refers back to envy in previous section, kept as impersonal force continuing through catalogue.
Passive of envy-verb shows Adam persuaded God envies him; preserves who envies whom.
Temporary stewardship image for widowed church before remarriage, not legal office.

choices.term: τῇ χήρᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνάνδρῳ τέως Ἐκκλησίᾳ
choices.why: Keeps both adjectives and temporal limit; uses glossary church.

pass_b_english: This same thing darkened the Morning Star, who fell through pride. Though he was divine, he could not bear not to be counted as God. This same thing drove Adam out of paradise, stealing him through pleasure and a woman. Kept for a time from the tree of knowledge, Adam was persuaded that he is begrudged being God. This same thing made Cain the murderer of his brother, for he could not bear a holier sacrifice. This same thing covered a disordered world with water and overwhelmed the people of Sodom with fire. This same thing buried Dathan and Abiram, who raged against Moses, and struck Miriam with leprosy, though she had only murmured against her brother. This same thing stained the earth with the blood of prophets and shook Solomon, the wisest of men, through women.

This same thing made Judas a traitor, stolen away for a little silver, a man worthy of the noose. This same thing made Herod a murderer of children and made Pilate a killer of Christ. This same thing winnowed Israel and scattered it, a sin from which its people have not risen even now. This same thing raised up against us the apostate tyrant, whose embers still pain us even now, though we have escaped the flame. This same thing cut apart the fair body of the church, dividing it into different and rival parties. This same thing has raised up against us our Jeroboam, the slave of sin, and lays a bond upon my tongue. For Jeroboam cannot bear the Trinity glorified, shining with the whole Godhead, and making her true heralds honored in your eyes. Do I seem to you to talk nonsense in drawing these parallels? Or has my written account rightly portrayed the causes of your love? On these matters, this is what I think.

Since I see some troubled by the insults against me, and making my dishonor into their own misfortune, come, let me reflect briefly on it in the spirit of the philosophical life. If I came to you with some petty human aim, laying claim to this see, and took authority over you with this gray hair and these limbs worn thin by time and sickness, or if I now bear this dishonor with such an aim, I would be ashamed before heaven and earth, by which even the ancients would swear. I would be ashamed before this see, and before this holy council, and before this holy and newly formed people, against whom so great a battle line of evil powers stands, to dissolve it before it holds together and to kill it before it is born, even as it is now being formed in Christ. I would be ashamed before my own toils and labors, before this threadbare clothing, and before the desert and the retreat where we lived together, before a life without comfort and a frugal table little better than the birds. Then let some speak the truth about me, that I desired another man's wife, though I refused to have a wife of my own. Then let even the Gibeonites have the advantage over me, whom I know the Holy Spirit does not admit even as woodcutters and water carriers, until they come to holy things with such stains on their life and speech. But if I came to plead for the faith, and to bring what help I could to the widowed and presently husbandless church, like caretakers and guardians who will give her in marriage to another, to one who proves worthy of her beauty and brings greater bridal gifts of virtue to the queen, then am I praiseworthy for my eagerness or blameworthy for what others suspect? For I am judged by passions that belong to others.

problems.quote: let the Gibeonites also get a hold on me
problems.source_quote: Ἐχέτωσαν δὲ ἡμῶν καὶ Γαβαωνῖται πλέον
problems.why: The Greek means let the Gibeonites have the advantage over me, since even they are barred from holy things. 'Get a hold on me' misses this and is unclear.
problems.fix: Then let even the Gibeonites have the advantage over me, whom I know the Holy Spirit does not admit even as woodcutters and water carriers.

edits.old: Then let the Gibeonites also get a hold on me
edits.new: Then let even the Gibeonites have the advantage over me

fixed: Fixed Gibeonites phrase: source Ἐχέτωσαν δὲ ἡμῶν καὶ Γαβαωνῖται πλέον means have the advantage over, not get a hold on.

last_rejected.quote: to dissolve it before it holds together and to kill it before it is born
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα πρὶν συστῆναι λυθῇ, καὶ πρὶν γεννηθῆναι νεκρωθῇ
last_rejected.why: The ἵνα clause is the evil powers' purpose: that the people be dissolved and die. English makes that Gregory's act.
last_rejected.fix: against whom so great a battle line of evil powers stands, that it may be broken up before it holds together and die before it is born
last_rejected.ruling: Passive λυθῇ/νεκρωθῇ takes the people as subject. English 'to dissolve it' follows 'battle line of evil powers stands', so it reads as the powers' purpose.

last_rejected.quote: If I came to you with some petty human aim, laying claim to this see, and took authority over you
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰ μὲν ἀνθρώπινόν τι καὶ μικρὸν ἐννοῶν, ἢ τῆς καθέδρας ταύτης μεταποιούμενος, ἢ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐπέστην ὑμῖν
last_rejected.why: ἤ marks alternative grounds of shame, and τὴν ἀρχήν means at the outset, not a further act of taking authority.
last_rejected.fix: If, thinking some petty human thought, or laying claim to this see, I at the outset was set over you
last_rejected.ruling: 'took authority over you' is loose for τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐπέστην, but 'laying claim to this see' already carries the idea. Gregory's denial of ambition is kept.

last_rejected.why: τρύχινον means a garment of hair, the ascetic hair shirt, not cloth worn thin.
last_rejected.ruling: τρύχινον comes from τρύχω, 'worn out, ragged'. 'Threadbare' fits; it does not mean hair-cloth.
